title: Capital Strategy
intro: Growth, acquisition or a change in ownership: compare the funding routes, sequence the decisions and understand what each option asks of you.
audience: Owners, boards and finance teams weighing a growth plan, acquisition, refinancing or ownership decision.
trigger: You know what the business wants to achieve, but need to decide how much capital, which structure and in what order.
scope: Review the objectives, current borrowing, ownership and planned use of funds
Compare debt and equity options against cash generation, control and future flexibility
Map funding dependencies, information gaps and the decisions needed before an approach
process: Set the decision
Agree the business objective, constraints and options to assess.
Compare the structures
Test funding routes against cash flow, ownership and the next capital requirement.
Agree the roadmap
Review trade-offs, priorities and the information needed before approaching providers.
prepare: The objective, use of funds and preferred timetable
A high-level view of trading, cash generation and existing borrowing
Current ownership, shareholder priorities and non-negotiable constraints
fees: Standalone advisory work is client-paid, with scope, deliverables and fees agreed before work starts. Funding introductions are paid for by funding providers; Frontier charges no client fee for that funding activity. Provider fees and costs may still apply.
boundaries: No assurance of funding, valuation or completion. Legal, tax, audit and other specialist advice requires appropriately qualified providers. Delivery responsibilities are agreed for each engagement.
faqs: Do we need to choose debt or equity first?
No. The engagement can compare both, including sequencing or a combination, without assuming either is available.
Can you review existing borrowing?
Yes, within an agreed scope: consider maturity, cost, security, covenants and how current obligations affect the plan.
Does the roadmap commit us to raising capital?
No. It supports a decision. You can engage Frontier for the strategy work independently of a funding introduction.
headline: Choose the capital before it shapes the business.
outputDescriptions: A sequenced view of the capital requirement, key decisions, dependencies and next actions.
A comparison of relevant structures, their commitments and the assumptions behind the shortlist.
A practical list of evidence needed to test the options and prepare the next conversation.

title: Funding Readiness
intro: Turn the business plan, numbers and supporting evidence into a coherent case before the lender or investor starts asking questions.
audience: Owners and management teams preparing an initial application, a refinancing or an investor conversation.
trigger: The funding requirement is emerging, but the information is incomplete, inconsistent or spread across several documents.
scope: Assess the proposed funding case and identify evidence gaps

fees: Standalone advisory work is client-paid, with scope, deliverables and fees agreed before work starts. Funding introductions are paid for by funding providers; Frontier charges no client fee for that funding activity. Provider fees and costs may still apply.
boundaries: No assurance of funding, valuation or completion. Legal, tax, audit and other specialist advice requires appropriately qualified providers. Delivery responsibilities are agreed for each engagement.
faqs: Can you help before we know which provider to approach?
Yes. Readiness work can start from the business requirement. Provider-specific forms can be scoped once a relevant route is identified.
Do you write business plans and presentations?
They can be included in the agreed deliverables. The engagement should specify which documents are being prepared and what input is required from you.
Does a completed pack mean an application will be approved?
No. A coherent pack helps a provider assess the case; it does not replace its criteria, diligence or decision.

title: Financial Modelling
intro: See where the plan needs cash—and what changes when assumptions move.
audience: Owners, finance directors and management teams assessing a project, funding round, acquisition or working-capital need.
trigger: The commercial plan is taking shape, but the cash requirement, repayment capacity or downside case needs testing.
scope: Integrated profit and loss, balance sheet and cash-flow forecasts
Working-capital assumptions, debt schedules and funding gaps
Project appraisal, affordability and scenario analysis
process: Scope the engagement
Agree the objective, inputs, deliverables and fee.
Develop the work
Review information and assumptions with the client.
Review and hand over
Explain outputs, limitations and the next decisions.
prepare: Your objective, intended decision and forecast horizon
Recent accounts, management figures and existing forecasts, if available
Trading assumptions, investment costs and current facility terms
fees: Standalone advisory work is client-paid, with scope, deliverables and fees agreed before work starts. Funding introductions are paid for by funding providers; Frontier charges no client fee for that funding activity. Provider fees and costs may still apply.
boundaries: No assurance of funding, valuation or completion. Legal, tax, audit and other specialist advice requires appropriately qualified providers. Delivery responsibilities are agreed for each engagement.
faqs: Do we need an existing model?
No. We can scope a new model or review and develop an existing one. The available records and decision determine the work.
Can you model a downside case?
Yes. Agree the variables to test—such as payment delays, costs, sales or programme timing—and compare cash requirements under those assumptions.
Does a model guarantee that funding will be available?
No. It is a decision tool based on assumptions, not an audit, valuation assurance or a funding commitment. A provider makes its own assessment.
headline: Put the numbers behind the next move.

audience: Established businesses, property sponsors and finance teams considering borrowing, refinancing or asset-backed funding.

faqs: Is this different from a funding introduction?
Yes. A separately commissioned advisory engagement covers agreed analysis or preparation. Frontier’s funding introductions are provider-paid, with no Frontier client fee for that funding activity.
Will you negotiate with lenders?
Commercial negotiation support can be agreed within scope. Providers decide their own offers and conditions; legal terms require appropriate legal advice.
Can you compare a facility we already have?
An existing facility can be included in a scoped comparison. Use consistent assumptions and check any consent, early repayment or security implications.

title: Equity & Strategic Capital
intro: Prepare the investment proposition, test dilution scenarios and align the round with the milestone and shareholder decisions ahead.
audience: Founders, boards and shareholders preparing venture, growth or strategic equity conversations.
trigger: You are planning a raise or ownership change and need the proposition, financial case and shareholder expectations to line up.

faqs: Will you tell us what the business is worth?
We can examine valuation assumptions and their implications within scope. This is not valuation assurance, and investors may reach different conclusions.
Can you help us understand dilution?
Yes. Agreed scenarios can show the ownership effects of different round assumptions. Rights, preferences and future funding also need attention.
Do you guarantee investor introductions or a completed round?
No. Any proposed approach depends on mandate and fit and requires your agreement. Investor interest, diligence and completion remain uncertain.

title: Due Diligence & Transactions
intro: Bring the information, advisers and open questions into one coordinated process, from diligence requests to completion milestones.
audience: Owners, finance teams and transaction leads managing a capital raise, acquisition, property transaction or complex funding process.
trigger: A transaction has several moving parts, but information requests, adviser actions and completion conditions need a single working view.

boundaries: No assurance of funding, valuation or completion. Legal, tax, audit and other specialist advice requires appropriately qualified providers. Delivery responsibilities are agreed for each engagement.
faqs: Does this replace legal or financial due diligence?
No. Frontier can provide scoped financial/commercial review and coordination. Legal, tax, audit and other specialist opinions remain with appropriately qualified providers.
Can you join a transaction already under way?
The engagement can be scoped around the current stage, open issues and responsibilities. We first need to understand what has been agreed and who owns each workstream.
Can you guarantee the completion date?
No. Diligence, counterparties, documentation and conditions can change the critical path. The timetable makes dependencies visible rather than removing them.
